Dashboard.QuickAction.Title: Quick action
Dashboard.QuickAction.Help: Moves or copies every file in the source folder (not recursive) to Destination — without having to create a folder/rule for it. Destination can contain variables (e.g. ..\{ModifiedYear}_{ModifiedMonth}\{OriginalName}.{OriginalExtension}) and is recomputed separately for every file. Use Modified rather than Created: Windows often resets the creation date to 'now' whenever a file is copied/downloaded, which would otherwise dump everything into the same folder. Source folder and Destination are remembered and pre-filled the next time FldrSrtr opens.

RuleEditor.Title: Rule editor
RuleEditor.VariableHelp.Intro: Variables for Destination/Arguments — click "Insert variable" on an action for the full menu, or type them here yourself:
RuleEditor.VariableHelp.Counter: Increases per file processed in this run; not remembered between runs.
RuleEditor.VariableHelp.Guid: A unique GUID, freshly generated every time.
RuleEditor.VariableHelp.Random: Random number — the pattern sets the digit count and zero-padding.
RuleEditor.VariableHelp.RandomString: Random text — the number after the colon is the length (default 8).
RuleEditor.VariableHelp.FileProps: Properties of the file itself (current name/path — changes along if an earlier action already renamed it).
RuleEditor.VariableHelp.Created.Warning: Note: Windows often resets this to 'now' as soon as a file is copied/downloaded — Modified is usually more reliable for the original date.
RuleEditor.VariableHelp.RunMoment: The moment the rule runs — the same for every file in this run.
RuleEditor.VariableHelp.UnixTimestamp: That same moment, as seconds/microseconds since 1970.
RuleEditor.VariableHelp.Example.Suffix: — a subfolder that doesn't exist yet is created automatically.
RuleEditor.ConditionsHelp: A group combines conditions or other groups: ALL = every one must match (AND), ANY = at least one must match (OR), NOT = the opposite (must NOT match). Groups can be nested for more complex logic, e.g. "extension is pdf AND (name contains 'invoice' OR name contains 'factuur')". Click a group to add a condition or a new (nested) group to it; click a condition to edit it.
RuleEditor.SelectGroupOrCondition: Select a group or condition above.
RuleEditor.AllFieldHint: Matches every file — no filter, no Operator/Value needed.
RuleEditor.DuplicateHint: Tip: for Field 'Duplicate', Value is 'true' or 'false'.
RuleEditor.SelectOrAddAction: Select an action on the left, or add one.
ActionHelp.Move: Moves the file to Destination. A folder that doesn't exist yet is created.
ActionHelp.Copy: Copies the file to Destination. The original stays where it is.
ActionHelp.Rename: Renames the file. Destination is the new file name (no path), e.g. {FileName}_archive.{Extension}.
ActionHelp.DeleteToRecycleBin: Moves the file to the Recycle Bin. No Destination needed.
ActionHelp.Open: Opens the file with Windows' default application. No Destination needed.
ActionHelp.OpenWith: Opens the file with the application at the path in Destination (e.g. C:\Apps\Reader.exe).
ActionHelp.ExecuteExternal: Runs the program/script in Destination. Arguments are the command-line parameters passed along, e.g. "{FullPath}" to pass the file's path.
ActionHelp.CreateFolder: Creates the folder in Destination if it doesn't exist yet (e.g. to pre-create an archive folder).
ActionHelp.AddExtension: Appends an extension to the file name. Destination is just the extension (no dot), e.g. 'bak' turns 'file.pdf' into 'file.pdf.bak'.
ActionHelp.RemoveExtension: Strips the current extension, e.g. 'file.pdf' -> 'file'. No Destination needed.
ActionHelp.Zip: Adds the file to the zip archive in Destination (created if it doesn't exist yet).
ActionHelp.DeleteTargetIfExists: Sends the file at Destination to the Recycle Bin, but only if it exists — otherwise nothing happens. Doesn't touch the file this rule is processing. Handy right before a Move/Copy to that same Destination.

IconOverrides.Title: Custom icons
IconOverrides.Intro: Optionally assign your own image (PNG) to each icon. Without a custom choice, the active icon set (Settings) is used, or the Default set if that doesn't have the icon either. 'Save as set...' saves the icons you see right now (your own choices plus the rest) as a new, reusable icon set in Settings.
